title: Tensor closure for bounded-above pseudo-coherent complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For integers $n,m$, suppose that $K$ is $n$-pseudo-coherent and $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>a$, while $L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j>b$ (where pseudo-coherence and its finite-stage variants are as in [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]). Here $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is the derived tensor product: the image in $D(R)$ of the direct-sum total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R L^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], for any K-flat complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] $P^\bullet$ with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K$ and any complex $L^\bullet$ representing $L$. Then $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is $t$-pseudo-coherent for $t=\max(m+a,n+b)$. In particular, the derived tensor of two pseudo-coherent objects is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: First record the upper-bound calculation used below. If $X,Y\in D(R)$ have cohomology zero above $u,v$, choose representing complexes and replace them by their good truncations $\tau_{\le u}X^\bullet,\tau_{\le v}Y^\bullet$. The truncation inclusions are quasi-isomorphisms, since they retain all the possibly nonzero cohomology. Apply the bounded-flat replacement statement on the one-object site with only the identity covering and structure ring $R$: ordinary $R$-modules identify with module sheaves on this site. It supplies flat complexes $F,G$, zero in degrees above $u,v$, respectively. They are K-flat by the bounded-flat criterion. The derived tensor is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R G)$. In degree $k>u+v$ each summand has $p>u$ or $q>v$ and is zero. Thus $H^k(X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y)=0$ for $k>u+v$. This is just the total-degree calculation after applying the cited replacements.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: Put $t=\max(m+a,n+b)$. If $n>a$, the preceding calculation gives vanishing of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ above $a+b<t$ because $t\ge n+b>a+b$. The map from the zero finite-free complex is therefore an isomorphism in degrees greater than $t$ and surjective in degree $t$. It witnesses $t$-pseudo-coherence. If $m>b$, use instead $t\ge m+a>a+b$ and the same zero witness. Hence it remains to treat $n\le a$ and $m\le b$.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: Choose bounded finite-free witnesses $\alpha:P^\bullet\to K$ and $\beta:Q^\bullet\to L$ from the definition of $n$- and $m$-pseudo-coherence. Write $C_\alpha,C_\beta$ for cone objects in distinguished triangles $P\to K\to C_\alpha\to P[1]$ and $Q\to L\to C_\beta\to Q[1]$, with $P,Q$ the images of the complexes in $D(R)$. The long exact sequences show $H^i(C_\alpha)=0$ for $i\ge n$ and $H^i(C_\beta)=0$ for $i\ge m$: in the segment $H^i(P)\to H^i(K)\to H^i(C_\alpha)\to H^{i+1}(P)\to H^{i+1}(K)$ the first arrow is surjective and the last is injective for $i\ge n$, and likewise for $\beta$. Also $H^j(Q)=0$ for $j>b$, since $j>b\ge m$ and $H^j(\beta)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: Apply the exact functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$ to the first cone triangle. The cone of $\alpha\otimes 1_Q:P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$ is $C_\alpha\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$, whose cohomology vanishes above $(n-1)+b$ by step 1. Next apply $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ to the second cone triangle. To write it in the desired factor order use the signed flip $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ for degrees $p,q$. It is its own inverse; the tensor differential formula gives equal coefficients $(-1)^{pq+q}$ on $y\otimes d x$ and $(-1)^{pq}$ on $d y\otimes x$ on both sides. This natural chain isomorphism descends through K-flat models. Thus the cone of $1_K\otimes\beta:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_\beta$, with cohomology zero above $a+(m-1)$ by step 1.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: For a triangle $A\xrightarrow f B\to C\to A[1]$ with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\ge t$, its long exact sequence makes $H^i(f)$ an isomorphism for $i>t$ and $H^t(f)$ surjective: the adjacent groups $H^{i-1}(C),H^i(C)$ vanish when $i>t$, and $H^t(C)=0$ suffices for surjectivity. In step 4 both cones vanish in degrees $i\ge t$, since $t\ge n+b$ and $t\ge m+a$. Each of the two maps is therefore an isomorphism above $t$ and surjective at $t$. Their composite $\alpha\otimes^{\mathbf L}\beta:P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ has the same properties, by functoriality of tensor and composition of surjections.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: Each finite-free module is flat: after a choice of finite basis its tensor functor is a finite direct sum of the identity functor, and exactness is checked coordinatewise. Hence the bounded complexes $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ are K-flat by the cited criterion, and $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$ is represented by $E^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R Q^\bullet)$. This is bounded and finite free in each degree. Indeed, for finite bases indexed by $I_p,J_q$, the tensors of their basis vectors indexed by $I_p\times J_q$ form a basis of $P^p\otimes_R Q^q$, with inverse sending each pure tensor to its coordinate products; the finite disjoint union over $p+q=k$ gives a finite basis of $E^k$. Bounds on the degrees of $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ give the sum of these bounds for $E^\bullet$. Together with step 5, the map $E^\bullet\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$ is the required witness in the definition of $t$-pseudo-coherence.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, proof of (1): details of the omitted tensor approximation argument

proof.text: For the final assertion, use the definition of pseudo-coherence to choose bounded-above finite-free representatives $F^\bullet,G^\bullet$ for $K,L$, with upper term bounds $c,d$. Finite-free modules are flat by the coordinate argument of step 6; hence both representatives are K-flat. Their total tensor represents the derived tensor. For each degree $k$, nonzero summands satisfy $k-d\le p\le c$ and $q=k-p$, so only finitely many summands occur, each finite free by the explicit tensor bases of step 6. The total complex is zero above $c+d$. Thus it is a bounded-above finite-free representative, proving pseudo-coherence directly from its definition, without a Noetherian or finite Tor-dimension assumption.
